system.title: System Information
tailscale.disconnectHelp: Disconnects this machine from your tailnet.
tailscale.connectHelp: Connects this machine to your tailnet.
appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.accentHelp: Applies across the app, in both light and dark.
scanning.title: Scanning
scanning.serviceDetectionHelp: Also check each device on a short list of well-known ports (web, printer, NAS, and so on) to identify it more precisely and flag a web interface. Sends a little more traffic and takes a little longer, so it is off by default. Applies on the next scan.
scanning.serviceDetectionTip: Deeper device identification via a light port probe
scanning.intervalHelp: How often the background scanner re-scans while continuous scan is on. Takes effect on the next cycle. Default: {default} seconds.
networks.title: Networks
networks.onlyListed: Scan only the networks I list
networks.onlyListedHelp: Ignore the auto-detected interfaces and scan only the "Networks to scan" list below. Useful on a host with many Docker bridges, VLANs, or routed interfaces.
networks.onlyListedTip: Scan only the networks you list, not the detected ones
networks.help: A routed network (reached through a router, not on a local interface) is scanned but has no MAC addresses. Applies on the next scan. Saved to this instance, not your config file.
groups.title: Device Groups
groups.intro: Rename a group to fit your own kit, or add ones that suit it better. Renaming updates every device already in that group. Deleting a group leaves its devices ungrouped, it never deletes a device.
groups.help: Changes apply immediately. Saved to this instance, not your config file.
locations.title: Locations
locations.intro: Where your devices are, shown in their own column on the dashboard. You can also type a new place straight into a device's Location field.
storage.title: Storage
storage.retentionHelp: A device not seen for this many days is removed. Devices you have labelled, grouped, or added notes to, and devices currently online, are always kept. 0 keeps them forever. Default: {default}.
storage.maxDevicesHelp: When the list grows past this, the devices seen longest ago are dropped first (labelled, grouped, noted, and online devices are kept). 0 means no cap. Default: {default}.
storage.help: Changes apply immediately: lowering these can remove stale devices right away. Saved to this instance, not your config file.
notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.help: Get a message when a device appears, goes missing or changes address. Telegram, Discord, Slack, ntfy and Home Assistant work by pasting their webhook URL.
notifications.urlHelp: Webhook URLs often contain a secret, so once saved only the start of the address is shown.
notifications.name: Name (optional)
notifications.telegramHelp: For Telegram, use {url}. Messages are sent in English.
security.title: Security
security.signOutHelp: Ends this session on this browser.
api.title: API access
api.intro: A token lets a script, a dashboard or an agent read your network without signing in through a browser.
api.copyNow: Copy this now. Only a hash of it is stored, so it cannot be shown again.
api.replaces: Creating another token replaces this one.
data.title: Data Management
data.exportHelp: A CSV of the device list, or a shareable, self-contained HTML report of the whole network.
data.restoreAsk: Restore {file}? This {strong}replaces{strongEnd} the current devices, settings, and snapshots on this instance.
data.backupHelp: Download a copy of your devices, settings, and snapshots (not your password) as a single file, or restore from one.
about.title: About
about.text: LAN Orangutan is a network discovery and monitoring tool that helps you keep track of devices on your local network.
scan.title: Scanning network...
api.accessOff: API tokens are turned off on this instance ({setting} in config.ini), so scripts cannot sign in with one. Turn it back on and restart to use the API.
